the-indolence-of-the-filipino: José Rizal answers the Spanish colonial charge that Filipinos are lazy in this brilliant 1890 essay. With history, economics, and wit, he shows that oppression — not character — explains his people's condition. A landmark of anti-colonial thought, as sharp today as when written.
c-sallusti-crispi-de-bello-catilinario-e: Sallust's immortal histories — the conspiracy of Catiline and the war with Jugurtha — in the original Latin. Rome's moral decline, painted by a master of terse and pointed style. The classic school text for students of Latin prose. His terse moral judgments still sting after two thousand years.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-mont: This article crowns Monte Cassino, St. Benedict's own mountain. The father of Western monks wrote his Rule there. Gilbert Huddleston honors the mother house. All monastic life flows from this rock. Bombardment in 1944 could not end its fourteen centuries. The Rule was written on this very mountain.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-albano: A 1913 entry on Albano — the suburbicarian see by the Alban lake. Ernesto Buonaiuti gives its history. Cardinals have held it since early days. The papal palace overlooks its waters. Rome's summer neighbor. Its cardinals elect the popes. Its lake mirrors the papal villa.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alberic-of-mo: This 1913 reference piece on Alberic of Monte Cassino — the cardinal of the Gregorian reform. Thomas Shahan honors his pen. He wrote against Berengar's error. Reform found a learned champion. A monk in the Church's great battle. His Dictatus defended the papal cause.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alessandro-bo: A 1913 entry on Alessandro Bonvicino — Moretto, the Brescian painter. Augustus Van Cleef praises his altarpieces. His saints glow with quiet devotion. Brescia's churches keep his best. A master of Lombard piety. His Saint Justina is a Lombard treasure. Titian admired his quiet art.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alonso-cano: A 1913 entry on Alonso Cano — the Spanish painter, sculptor, and architect. Leigh Hunt sketches his stormy genius. His Virgins glow with tender grace. Granada's cathedral keeps his works. Andalusia's universal artist. His cathedral facade crowns Granada. His drawings fill the Madrid collections.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ambrogio-cale: A 1913 entry on Ambrogio Calepino — Calepinus, the dictionary maker. Charles Dubray honors his great lexicon. His Latin wordbook served for centuries. Every schoolboy knew his name. The dictionary's Augustinian father. His name became the word for dictionary. His folios lined the college shelves.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-andrea-castag: This 1913 reference piece on Andrea Castagno — the stern Florentine painter. Louis Gillet praises his frescoes. His Last Supper fills Sant'Apollonia. Strength marks his rugged saints. Florence's iron draughtsman. His equestrian portraits line the villa. His sibyls adorn the cathedral dome.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-andrea-cesalp: A 1913 entry on Andrea Cesalpino — the botanist and physician. Josef Rompel honors his science. His plant system led to Linnaeus. Pisa's garden grew under him. A doctor among the naturalists. His herbs fill the Pisa garden. His pulse studies aided Harvey.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-andrea-contuc: A 1913 entry on Andrea Sansovino — the sculptor of the sweet style. Gerhard Gietmann honors his marble. His tombs grace Santa Maria del Popolo. Rome and Loreto keep his best. The gentle master of the chisel. His Baptist stands in the Florentine baptistery.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-andrea-pisano: A 1913 entry on Andrea Pisano — the sculptor of the baptistery doors. John Joseph A'Becket praises his bronze. His south doors show the Baptist's life. Giotto designed his campanile reliefs. Florence's gentle Gothic master. His Venice panels show his grace. His tabernacle graces Or San Michele.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-angel-de-saav: This 1913 reference piece on the Duke of Rivas — Ángel de Saavedra, Spain's Romantic poet. Ventura Fuentes honors his Don Alvaro. His verse broke the classic chains. Exile taught him liberty's price. Spain's Romantic pioneer. His plays founded the Spanish Romantic stage.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antonio-di-ma: A 1913 entry on Antonio Rossellino — the Florentine sculptor of sweetness. Marie Louise Handley praises his marble. His tombs grace the Tuscan churches. Grace marks his every figure. The gentle chisel of the Renaissance. His Cardinal's tomb graces San Miniato. His busts line the Bargello's halls.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antonio-monte: A 1913 entry on Antonio Montesino — the Dominican voice of the oppressed Indians. Henry Schroeder honors his 1511 sermon. His Advent cry shook Hispaniola. Las Casas took up his cause. The first cry for Indian rights. His sermon is the missions' charter.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ariano: This 1913 reference piece on Ariano — the Irpinian diocese of the hill town. Ernesto Buonaiuti gives its story. Its bishops serve the Apennine parishes. The Norman castle crowns its height. A see of the southern mountains. Its majolica graces the local churches.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ascendente-do: This 1913 reference piece on Ascendente Domino — a papal constitution. Michael O'Riordan explains its terms. The entry sets out its canonical force. The curia's acts shaped the Church's life. A document of the Holy See. Its text is the canonists' reference.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ascoli-piceno: This 1913 reference piece on Ascoli Piceno — the Marchigian diocese of the travertine town. Ernesto Buonaiuti gives its story. Its bishops date from antiquity. The Tronto river guards its walls. A see of the central hills. Its Piazza del Popolo charms visitors.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-avellino: A 1913 entry on Avellino — the Irpinian diocese of the hill town. Ernesto Buonaiuti gives its story. Its bishops serve the mountain parishes. The Partenio guards its valley. A see of the Campanian hills. Its cathedral keeps the old relics. Its hazelnuts are famed through Italy.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-basle-lugano: A 1913 entry on Basle-Lugano — the united Swiss diocese. Joseph Lins gives its story. Its bishops serve the two cantons. The Reformation divided its flock. A diocese of the Alpine border. Its bishops serve the two tongues. Its seminary trains the mountain priests.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-benedetto-da-: A 1913 entry on Benedetto da Majano — the Florentine sculptor architect. Marie Louise Handley praises his marble. His Strozzi palace crowns the city. The pulpit of Santa Croce is his. The gentle master of the chisel. His Annunciation graces the Arezzo church.

This 1913 reference article on Benedetto da Rovezzano — the sculptor of the Medici tombs. Marie Louise Handley notes his English exile. His works grace the Florentine churches. The entry preserves his modest fame. A master of the marble tomb. His Cardinal Wolsey tomb was famed.
